title: Search in Rotated Sorted Array
description: There is an integer array nums sorted in ascending order (with distinct values), possibly rotated at an unknown pivot. Given the array after the rotation and an integer target, return the index of target if it is in nums, or -1 if it is not. You must write an algorithm with O(log n) runtime complexity.
constraints: All values of nums are unique
hints: At each step, at least one half of the array (left of mid, or right of mid) is guaranteed to be normally sorted — figure out which half that is, then check if target falls in that half's range.

optimalSolution.approach: Modified binary search: at each mid, determine which half (left or right of mid) is normally sorted by comparing nums[lo] to nums[mid], then check whether target lies within that sorted half's range to decide which side to keep searching.

followUpQuestions: How would this change if the array could contain duplicate values?
Can you first find the rotation pivot with binary search, then do a normal binary search?
Why does a plain binary search break down here without the extra sorted-half check?
interviewerNotes: Tests whether a candidate can adapt a known pattern (binary search) to a modified invariant rather than just reciting the textbook version. The duplicates follow-up (LC 81) is a good escalation for a strong candidate.
